elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 states that Customer “is not required to disclose” any more favourable commercial offer, and §12.3 confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match or extend to Vendor more favourable commercial terms offered by another provider.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 states that Customer “is not required to…match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer is limited to a defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no MFN obligation on Customer, as confirmed by §§7.2 and 12.3. Therefore no broader-than-product MFN burden exists.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: Customer has no MFN obligation, so there is no MFN burden extending beyond 12 months.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer includes reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: Customer has no MFN obligation requiring comparison of third-party offers, so no unreasonable-comparison burden applies.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates both disclosure and matching duties, and §12.3 independently confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. This fully satisfies the preferred position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied because their condition—an MFN burden on Customer—is demonstrably absent. The amendment is narrowly targeted and leaves unrelated commercial terms unchanged, although §7.2 would read more cleanly as an unconditional statement that Customer has no disclosure or matching obligation rather than retaining the unnecessary “Before engaging another provider” lead-in.
